description: An exhaustive switch over a five-member string-literal union, one case per value. Repetitive-LOOKING, but this is the correct, idiomatic pattern for an exhaustively-checked union in TypeScript — not a maintainability defect, and must not be escalated into a refactor suggestion or a finding of any kind.
explanation: This is the code-quality analogue of a security false-positive trap: the fixture LOOKS like it could be flagged (five similar-shaped case blocks, a shallow 'repetition' pattern-matcher's favorite target) but is actually the correct, TypeScript-exhaustiveness-checked idiom for mapping a literal union to display strings — converting it to a lookup object would not fix a defect, because there isn't one; it would just be a different, equally-valid style. A reviewer that suggests refactoring this into 'a lookup table to reduce repetition' is manufacturing a style preference into a finding, exactly the escalation this fixture exists to catch. Paired with maintainability-01, which IS a genuine duplication defect, so the benchmark can tell 'the reviewer recognizes real duplication' apart from 'the reviewer flags anything that merely looks repetitive.'
